dedupe_keys.name: statistics canada food insecurity by economic family type canadian income survey 2018 to 2024

description: This table measures how many Canadians live in households that cannot reliably get enough food, broken down by type of family, and is the official annual series on household food insecurity in Canada. It is published by Statistics Canada from the Canadian Income Survey. Coverage is Canada, its regions and each province from 2018 to 2024, with the latest release in April 2026. Each row gives a reference year, a geography, an economic family type and a household food security status, with the number and share of persons. The whole table is available as a free download in CSV or SDMX form under the Statistics Canada Open Licence. Caveats: results are provincial and national survey estimates with sampling error, family types are broad, and the series starts only in 2018. Simulation uses: sizing the population that depends on food banks and emergency food assistance, and weighting vulnerable households in disaster food supply and relief distribution scenarios. Related records: the HungerCount survey (data-food-banks-canada-hungercount) counts actual food bank visits, and the USDA food security supplement (data-usda-cps-food-security-supplement) uses the same survey module in the United States.
